channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: China-Central Asia Transport Links Expanding Rapidly, Report Shows
item.description: A Eurasian Development Bank report indicates rapid growth in connectivity between China and Central Asia from 2020-2025. In 2025, 51 million tons of freight moved between the regions by rail and road. Infrastructure expansion, like the Bakhty-Ayagoz railway in Kazakhstan, is facilitating this growth, with further improvements in traffic management and logistics planned.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Fines for Foreigners Violating Labor Rules
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to impose fines on foreign citizens who violate labor regulations. Individuals who repeatedly commit administrative offenses or fail to pay fines may face deportation and a three-year ban on entering the country.

item.title: Afghanistan Futsal Team Players Invited for Friendlies Against Russia and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The Afghanistan Football Federation has invited 23 players for friendly matches against Russia and Kyrgyzstan. The team will train in Tehran from December 1 to 6, then play Russia from December 6 to 10. Fifteen players will be selected for the Kyrgyzstan matches from December 10 to 14.

item.title: Kazakhstan Simplifies Accreditation Process for Entrepreneurs and Laboratories
item.description: Kazakhstan is simplifying its accreditation procedures to improve services for entrepreneurs and laboratories. The changes include remote inspections and the launch of a Telegram bot for faster application processing. The National Accreditation Center is also identifying needed laboratory types and plans to use AI in the future.

item.title: Taliban Detain 10 Residents in Panjshir After Mine Explosion
item.description: Local sources in Panjshir report that Taliban intelligence arrested 10 residents after a mine explosion in the Rkha district. The explosion occurred near a school and a former minister's house. The alleged bomber died in the blast, but the Taliban accused local residents of involvement.

item.title: Israel Strikes Gaza Clinic; Two Doctors Without Borders Staff Killed
item.description: Doctors Without Borders announced two of its staff members were killed in an Israeli airstrike on a clinic in Gaza City. The strike occurred despite a ceasefire. Israel claims the deceased were Hamas members involved in military activities. The WHO condemned the attack.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Fines and Deportations for Illegal Foreign Labor
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan approved a bill on November 28 to increase penalties for foreign citizens working illegally. The amendments to the Code of Administrative Offenses introduce fines and potential deportation for those working without permits or engaging in unauthorized activities. Repeat offenders may face a three-year entry ban.

item.title: Kunar Explosion Kills at Least 10, Injures 110, Taliban Say
item.description: The Taliban's information and culture department in Kunar reported at least 10 killed and 110 injured in an explosion near a school in the provincial capital. Local sources claim the blast, which occurred in a house used by a Pakistani Taliban member to store explosives, killed at least 30 and injured 126, mostly students.

item.title: Taliban: Only 8 Kilometers of TAPI Pipeline Construction Remaining in Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Mines and Petroleum reports that 142.9 km of the TAPI pipeline have been laid in Afghanistan, with only 8 km left. Significant progress has also been made on related facilities. The ministry aims to complete the project by the end of the current year.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts Houthi Missile Targeting Riyadh; Yemen Conflict Escalates
item.description: Saudi Arabia announced on Saturday the interception of a cruise missile fired by Iran-backed Houthis towards Riyadh. Simultaneously, Houthi media reported 13 people injured in Saudi airstrikes on Sana'a. These exchanges follow a Houthi attack on a Saudi oil facility. The conflict has resulted in thousands of casualties and displacements.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prosecutors Recover 2.3 Trillion Som in Damages, Restore Rights
item.description: Uzbekistan's prosecutors have recovered 2.3 trillion som in damages during investigations and preliminary inquiries. They have also restored the violated rights of over 560,000 citizens and provided practical assistance to more than 30,000 entrepreneurs and foreign investors.

item.title: Kazakhstan Finishes Second in Group, to Face Iran for World Championship Berth
item.description: Kazakhstan's women's handball team lost to South Korea 34:20 in the final group match of the Asian Championship in Almaty. They will now compete against Iran for a spot in the 2027 World Championship in Hungary. Despite the loss, the Kazakh team showed effort against the 16-time Asian champions.

item.title: Uzbek Religious Blogger Mubashshir Ahmad's Case to be Heard in Cassation
item.description: The case of Alisher Tursunov, known as religious blogger Mubashshir Ahmad, will be heard in cassation by the Tashkent City Court on December 3. His lawyer stated that the appeal is being filed within the one-year limit for reviewing convictions that could worsen the convicted person's situation. The court session will be open.

item.title: Ibragimova and Seilkhan Secure Medals for Kazakhstan at Boxing World Cup Final
item.description: Karina Ibragimova and Oner Seilkhan have guaranteed at least bronze medals for Kazakhstan at the World Boxing Cup final in Tashkent. Ibragimova defeated an Olympic medalist, and Seilkhan, a youth world champion, overcame Kyrgyzstan's Almaz Orozbekov. Three other Kazakh boxers also advanced to the semi-finals.

item.title: Taliban Say 10 Killed, 110 Injured in Blast Near Kunar School
item.description: An explosion near a school in Kunar province killed 10 people and injured 110, according to the Taliban government. The blast occurred in a house storing explosives for mining and road projects. Investigations into the incident, attributed to negligence, are underway.

item.title: Almaty Opens New Highway to BAKAD to Reduce Traffic Congestion
item.description: Almaty is preparing to open a new highway connecting the Boroldai settlement to the Big Almaty Ring Road (BAKAD). Expected to open by December 2026, the road aims to divert 15-20% of traffic from Saina Street, significantly reducing travel time.

item.title: Human Rights Defender Raises New Concerns in Mubashshir Ahmad Case Ahead of Appeal
item.description: A human rights defender has highlighted new circumstances in the case of Mubashshir Ahmad (Alisher Tursunov) before a cassation hearing on December 3rd. He suggests Ahmad may not have returned to Uzbekistan voluntarily, citing a conversation with Ahmad's relatives about his passport being left behind.

item.title: Reduced Humanitarian Aid to Afghanistan Leads to Long Food Queues
item.description: Images from Jaghori district in Ghazni province show long queues for food aid, with residents reporting a decrease compared to previous years. The World Food Programme distributes aid every six months, a reduction from monthly distributions. UN agencies cite budget shortfalls for humanitarian operations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Taekwondo Athlete Secures Silver Medal at Grand Prix Final
item.description: Kazakhstan's Batyrkhan Toleugali won a silver medal in the taekwondo Grand Prix final in Astana, losing the 80kg final to Iran's Radin Zeinali 1-2. This marks Kazakhstan's first Grand Prix final appearance in seven years.

item.title: UN: 7.3 Million Afghans Benefit from UNDP Infrastructure Projects
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Afghanistan has announced that 7.3 million people have benefited from its Abadi Programme, which has constructed or rehabilitated 3,000 infrastructure facilities. Implemented between January 2022 and September 2026, the program aims to strengthen local communities' capacity to cope with crises by improving essential infrastructure and access to services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Rules for Drug and Psychotropic Substance Testing of Civil Servants
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved new rules for testing civil servants for drug and psychotropic substance use. The Ministry of Health and the Agency for Civil Service Affairs developed the order. The rules outline observation of employee behavior for signs of substance abuse, with procedures for testing and disciplinary action.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Criminal Liability for Deliberate Evasion of Customs Duties
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate approved amendments introducing criminal liability for intentionally evading customs duties. The changes aim to create a transparent environment for honest businesses while preventing illegal economic advantages. In 2023, 207 cases of evasion totaling 218 billion UZS were identified.

item.title: Suspect Detained in Almaty Arson Case Resulting in Five Deaths, Including Two Uzbek Citizens
item.description: A 37-year-old woman has been detained in Almaty on suspicion of intentionally setting fire to a private home, an act that resulted in the deaths of five people. Among the victims were two citizens of Uzbekistan and a child. Police believe personal animosity was the motive behind the arson. The fire occurred on November 26th.

item.title: Almaty Hosts Discussion on Role and Future of Maslikhats Amid Constitutional Reform
item.description: An expert meeting in Almaty discussed the role and future of local representative bodies (maslikhats) in light of constitutional reform. Participants examined the current electoral system, the independence of campaigns, and the maslikhats' function in representing regional interests and addressing public concerns.

item.title: Cannavaro Discusses Future with Uzbekistan National Team Management
item.description: Fabio Cannavaro stated he needs to discuss his future with the management of the Uzbekistan Football Association (UFA). In an interview with Italy's La Gazzetta dello Sport, he also commented on player Abdukodir Khusanov and the national team's performance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Law on Mobilization Preparation and Mobilization
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan has approved a law on "Mobilization Preparation and Mobilization." The legislation outlines how the state should prepare for potential military threats and ensure the country's functioning during mobilization. It covers not only military conscription but also the mobilization of economic, transport, and healthcare resources.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Traffic Restrictions Based on License Plate Numbers to Improve Air Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ecology Committee has proposed temporary restrictions on vehicle movement, including odd-even license plate days, during periods of poor air quality. The measures aim to implement the 'Clean Air' national project, with exceptions for electric vehicles and special transport.

item.title: Police arrest suspect in fatal house fire in Almaty
item.description: Police have arrested a 37-year-old woman suspected of intentionally setting fire to a private house in Almaty's Bostandyk district. The blaze resulted in the deaths of five people. The suspect has been placed in a temporary detention facility.

item.title: Herat section of TAPI gas pipeline project nears completion
item.description: Construction on the Herat section of the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline project is nearing completion, with 92% of the work finished. Approximately 142.9 kilometers of the 150-kilometer pipeline have been laid and welded. Installation of equipment and construction of related facilities are also progressing significantly.

item.title: Uzbekistan may grant tax and credit benefits to citizens called up for military service during mobilization
item.description: A draft law in Uzbekistan proposes tax and other mandatory payment exemptions for citizens called up for military service during mobilization. It also suggests deferring credit payment deadlines and preserving employment for mobilized citizens. The bill aims to provide financial relief and support.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Enhances Sanctions Control, Tax Service Gains New Powers
item.description: Starting December 5, 2026, Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service can suspend businesses' access to electronic invoices and deregister cash registers if sanctions risks are identified. The government approved six grounds for suspension, including fictitious supplies and lack of export confirmation, to bolster economic and financial stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Secures Two Golds at Astana Para Taekwondo Grand Prix Finals
item.description: Uzbekistan claimed two gold and three silver medals at the Astana Para Taekwondo Grand Prix Finals. Guljonoy Naimova and Asadbek Toshtemirov won gold in their respective categories. Kazakhstan's para taekwondo athletes were eliminated in the quarterfinals. The event is a qualifier for the 2028 Paralympic Games.

item.title: Explosion Near Afghan School Kills Seven Students, Wounds Nearly 100
item.description: An explosion near a secondary school in Afghanistan's Kunar province has resulted in the deaths of seven students and injured up to 99 others, according to Reuters citing Taliban interior ministry spokesman Abdul Matin Qani. Local media reported significantly higher casualties, with some sources indicating at least 25 dead and 50 wounded. The exact location and circumstances of the blast remain unclear, with investigations underway.

item.title: Land Dispute in Uruzgan Province Results in Two Deaths, Two Wounded
item.description: Two people were killed and two others injured in a land dispute between two families in the Dehrawud District of Uruzgan Province, according to Bilal Uruzgani, spokesperson for the Taliban's provincial police command. The incident occurred on Friday, November 27, when members of one family opened fire on the other during the dispute. This follows similar clashes in the province that have also resulted in casualties.

item.title: Tajikistan U-17 Team Faces Italy in World Cup Round of 16
item.description: Tajikistan's U-17 national football team will play Italy in the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup in Qatar. This marks the team's first knockout stage appearance in 19 years. Tajikistan advanced after securing a draw against Senegal in their final group match.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Invest Trillions of Tenge in Transit Corridor Upgrades
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate over 2 trillion tenge for the development of transit road corridors within the next three years. The Ministry of Transport detailed plans to improve routes like "Aktobe – Kyzylorda" and "Beyneu – Saksaulsky." Additionally, 37 border crossing points within the EAEU will be modernized by 2027 to double throughput capacity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Bill to Extend Land Lease Period to 49 Years
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis has approved a bill to systematize land rights, extending the maximum land lease period to 49 years. The amendments aim to simplify land use as a market asset, prevent illegal seizures, and clarify conditions for using and consolidating land plots. The law also enhances penalties for landowners and tenants who fail to prevent land encroachment.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Almaty Arson Case That Killed Five, Including Two Uzbek Citizens
item.description: A 37-year-old woman has been detained in Almaty as a suspect in a house fire that killed five people, including two Uzbek citizens. Police identified her through surveillance footage. Investigators believe the fire was intentionally set due to personal animosity. The suspect is in custody pending further investigation.

item.title: Woman Arrested in Connection with Deadly Almaty Fire That Killed Five
item.description: A 37-year-old woman has been arrested in Almaty in connection with a fatal fire that claimed the lives of five people, including a minor. Police suspect the fire was intentionally set due to a personal dispute. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Foreign Students at Unaccredited Kyrgyz Medical Schools Given One Month to Transfer
item.description: Foreign students at unaccredited medical universities in Kyrgyzstan will have 30 days to transfer to other institutions. They can re-register their visas without leaving the country. The government has tasked ministries with facilitating the transfer process.
